items.title: Accelerating the pace of Nigeria’s economic development
items.description: By Zubairu Usman Sadiq To the extent that an average Nigerian finds it difficult to meet the basic needs of food, shelter, clothing, health and protection, and the three core values of development; sustenance, self-esteem and freedom, development is still a mirage to us as a people and as a country, for how can one live a fulfilled life without these items? In as much as the factors and the process that ensures growth, progress, development and prosperity are yet to be concertized, Nigeria, the widely acclaimed giant of Africa remains perpetually potentially great, despite its vast, overwhelming and intimidating mineral, natural and human resources, regardless of the standard and benchmark for assessment. Nigerian is confronted by longstanding issues of corruption, mismanagement of resources, unprecedented economic hardship that has left millions of its citizens struggling to make ends meet. Not only that, the country continues to battle many social and economic challenges of insecurity such as banditry, kidnappings in the north-west region, insurgency by terrorist groups in the north-east, and separatist agitations in the south-east. Unemployment rate is not abating, and inflation is making life miserable for ordinary Nigerians as they find it increasingly difficult to afford basic necessities. Nigerians are struggling to put food on the table, with access to healthcare and education becoming more of a luxury than a right. The economic hardship has left many families in dire straits. The economic crisis Nigeria is facing at the moment is horrifying and frightening, such that urgent and sustainable attention and action is required. Government have introduced and already implementing comprehensive reforms, policies and strategies to address the economic hardship plaguing the nation, stimulate economic growth, reduce poverty, and create a more equitable society. It is imperative and mandatory for government to move in that direction, imperative to step up and lend a helping hand, particularly to the needy and the less privileged. The nation’s heavy reliance on oil exports has made it susceptible to fluctuations in global oil prices. When oil prices plummeted, Nigeria’s revenue stream took a massive hit. Prior to the coming of the present administration, petroleum products were subsidized, opening the subsidy regime to unmitigated fraud and corrupt practices. Removal of subsidies on petroleum products and floating of the currency, though causing untold hardship on Nigerians at the moment are good policy decisions, which is expected to begin to yield positive outcomes in no distant future. Government should however address more frontally the major obstacles to development such as inadequate capital investment, a crushing level of debt, poor terms of trade and inadequate technology. Corruption and inefficiency in government, large growing populations, high levels of poverty, large population of out-of-school children, inadequate infrastructure, insufficient economic diversification, and regional instability are inhibiting barriers to economic development the government must address and resolve, as much as possible. Government should look into diversification of the economy beyond oil, and establish of a social safety net to protect vulnerable citizens. There must be unwavering commitment to transparency and accountability to tackle corruption and mismanagement of public funds, which have long hindered progress. Government must be commended for its efforts at investments in infrastructure development. Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Highway, Port Harcourt-Aba Railway, rehabilitation and reconstruction of roads across the country are commendable actions. Also commendable are policies introduced to reflate and put the economy on a sound footing. We however call for a more pragmatic approach in addressing the harsh realities in the country. Issues of inflation, rising cost of living, increasing unemployment, high rate of poverty, widening income gaps, weak economic growth and several others should be more aggressively tackled. The energy sector needs more attention. Nigerians are groaning in darkness. Unemployment should be tackled with innovation and creativity. The private sector, entrepreneurs and critical stakeholders in the economy can create job opportunities through investments and expansion; thus, contributing to reducing the alarming unemployment rate in the country and help to strengthen the economy. Housing shortage and infrastructure deficit offers huge opportunities for investment. More investment in these critical areas would significantly enhance the nations GPD and national economic development. In other words, government should pay special attention to housing development and provision of affordable housing for the low- and medium-income earners, for the less privileged and vulnerable people in Nigeria. To effectively tackle Nigeria’s current economic hardship, government must collaborate with the organized private sector, professional organizations and critical stakeholders in the polity. The government should create an enabling environment for collaborative efforts, offering incentives to encourage private sector support for social causes. Government must engage Estate Surveyors and Valuers in all aspects within the scope of our professional functions. I can assure you that Nigeria would get the best from Estate Surveyors and Valuers if it focuses on the fundamental issue of how to unlock and harness the power and potentials of real estate for GDP enhancement, wealth creation and sustainable economic development of the nation, especially in its trillion dollar GDP dream. The post Accelerating the pace of Nigeria’s economic development appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Inflation seen slowing to 10.75pc in September
items.description: KARACHI: Some stakeholders and analysts expect inflation in September to slow despite the high uncertainty caused by the ongoing Gulf war. The financial sector expects oil prices to remain between $90 and $100 per barrel during the remaining days of September and in October. However, the situation has once again changed after US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that he had rejected Iran’s proposal for the Gulf war. Iran is now anticipating possible attacks from the US, raising concerns that oil prices could surge. Analysts expect oil prices to remain around $100 per barrel if the war resumes. However, much will depend on the availability of oil supplies in the international market. Pakistan imports 70pc of its oil and gas requirements, making inflation highly sensitive to oil prices. Stakeholders believe oil prices to hover around $100 per barrel Pakistan’s official headline inflation rose sharply to 11.1pc year-on-year in August 2026, up from 9.2pc in July 2026. According to a Topline Securities report, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for September is expected to rise 10.25-10.75pc year-on-year, down from 11.1pc in August. This projection is slightly lower than the August figure, but does not represent a significant decline. Petroleum prices have been rising daily in Pakistan and have now reached the highest level in the region. India increased petrol prices by 10pc, while Bangladesh reportedly jacked up by 16pc and Pakistan by over 50pc. “It is not easy to assess the exact inflation figure for September as oil prices have been changing both internationally and locally. We can only expect slightly lower inflation, with a fear that it may remain close to last month’s level,” said S.S. Iqbal, a money market expert. With inflation expected to remain at 10.25-10.75pc in September 2026, real interest rates are likely to stand at 75-125 basis points, lower than Pakistan’s historical average of 200-300 basis points, according to the Topline report. Electricity, housing, food and construction costs have also witnessed increases, suggesting that inflation could come in above analysts’ expectations, particularly if the Gulf war continues for an extended period. At the same time, Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia are preparing to respond to a possible new conflict involving the Houthis and the kingdom, adding to uncertainty over oil prices and supplies. Any disruption could have a direct impact on Pakistan’s economy and inflation. Pakistan’s foreign exchange reserves, currently exceeding $21.4 billion, may provide some cushion against higher oil import costs. However, they cannot prevent inflationary pressures from rising if the conflict continues and international energy prices remain elevated. Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

items.title: Maricarmen fuerza un giro del Gobierno y sus socios sobre vivienda
items.description: Para ella llega tarde, porque su desahucio ya se ha ejecutado y se ha quedado sin casa. Pero Maricarmen Abascal, a sus 87 años y con una imagen de total fragilidad en su silla de ruedas, parece estar a punto de lograr un imposible: los grupos de la mayoría de investidura, que llevaban meses de batalla sin solución a la vista, parecen ahora forzados a encontrar un acuerdo y dar un giro a la política de vivienda este martes con un decreto pactado entre todos. A la presión de la propia Maricarmen se sumó este sábado una manifestación masiva que interpeló sobre todo a Isabel Díaz Ayuso, presidenta de Madrid, a José Luis Martínez Almeida, alcalde de la ciudad, responsables de dar soluciones a la anciana, pero también a Pedro Sánchez y su Gobierno, exigiéndoles que este martes aprueben un decreto potente para impedir que haya más Maricarmenes. La presión es tan fuerte que es difícil pensar que se frustre esta vez el acuerdo, aunque tampoco es imposible porque las posiciones son contradictorias y hay vetos cruzados. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los Alonso no quieren ser llamados buitres
items.description: Ricardo Alonso Fernández y Fernando Alonso Fuentes, los administradores de Urbagestión, no quieren ser calificados como “fondo buitre”. Seguro que saben de quienes hablo, pero, por si acaso, les resumo que es la empresa inmobiliaria que lleva siete años intentando echar a Maricarmen (una octogenaria en silla de ruedas) del piso en el que vivía desde 1956. Proeza que Urbagestión por fin consiguió perpetrar hace cuatro días, con la armoniosa ayuda de las instituciones de este país, esto es, de la policía que acudió a tirar la puerta abajo y a zurrar a los manifestantes, y de la judicatura, en concreto de la magistrada Elena Cortina Blanco. Como señalaba acertadamente Pablo Ordaz el otro día, lo más formidable del asunto es que toda esta brutalidad es por completo legal. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El hartazgo no cabe en un decreto
items.description: La imagen de Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 años, acompañada por los antidisturbios mientras era desalojada en camilla de su casa en Madrid por una orden judicial, ha devuelto de golpe a la sociedad española a los momentos más duros de la crisis financiera de 2008, aquellos en los que se ejecutaron miles de desahucios de familias incapaces de pagar la hipoteca de su residencia habitual. Esa imagen ha catalizado el profundo malestar ante el problema de la vivienda, del que no escapan ni los mayores como Maricarmen ni los más jóvenes, ni tampoco una clase media cada vez más excluida de los beneficios de la economía que presume de ser la alumna aventajada de Europa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: De Pepi a Maricarmen siete años después: dos mujeres vulnerables y dos desahucios que movieron cambios legislativos
items.description: Maricarmen levanta la vista. Es lunes y faltan apenas 48 horas para que se ejecute su desahucio. Tiene 87 años. Hace siete que le llegó un primer burofax que le avisaba del peligro a la vista, quedarse en la calle, fuera de la casa donde ha vivido durante siete décadas. Su salud se ha debilitado en los últimos meses, le cuesta respirar, andar, necesita una silla de ruedas para moverse. Cuando llega el día, la sacan en camilla de su casa luego de haber escuchado durante horas los gritos y los golpes de la policía contra quienes actuaban en su defensa y trataban de impedir el desahucio. Duerme esa noche agotada en un hospital. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El desahucio de Maricarmen y el decreto de vivienda: cómo actuar en un mercado dominado por particulares
items.description: El desahucio de Maricarmen tiene como protagonista a una sociedad inmobiliaria, Urbagestión , propietaria del piso de Madrid en el que esta mujer de 87 años vivió siete décadas hasta ser expulsada por la fuerza. El caso pone el foco sobre quién está detrás de las casas que se alquilan en España, una de las cuestiones centrales del mercado y clave a la hora de definir las medidas que están negociándose para dar luz verde al próximo decreto de vivienda . Y la respuesta que ofrecen las estadísticas oficiales es menos sencilla de lo que puede parecer. Las empresas, fondos buitre y otros propietarios jurídicos representan una parte minoritaria del alquiler residencial, con un peso inferior al 10% . La mayor parte está en manos de personas físicas, caseras de aproximadamente el 25% de los hogares de España. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Disección del desahucio de Maricarmen: ¿podría haber sido diferente?
items.description: A Maricarmen la han intentado desahuciar cuatro veces. La última, lo han conseguido. Hace cuatro días que duerme en una cama de hospital , lejos de la que ha sido su casa durante siete décadas. La empresa Urbagestión compró su piso de Retiro (Madrid) en 2018 por un precio irrisorio para la zona precisamente porque ella vivía en él. Con una pensión de 1.400 euros, ella nunca ha dejado de pagar el alquiler, de renta antigua, y las facturas, unos 500 euros al mes en total. En 2020 los propietarios le dijeron que debía dejar el piso, porque el contrato ya había sido subrogado dos veces. Y desde entonces no han aceptado ninguna de las propuestas que han recibido —de la Administración, de particulares, de personalidades de la cultura— para o bien pagar la diferencia del alquiler (le pedían 1.600 euros) o comprar el apartamento. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La idea de expropiar pisos en Berlín agita la política alemana
items.description: Las estadísticas pueden ser una manera fría pero efectiva de entender grandes problemas. La crisis de la vivienda en Berlín es uno de estos casos: alquilar un apartamento en la capital de Alemania se encareció un 69% entre 2016 y 2026, según datos del Gobierno federal. Si hace 10 años alquilar un piso de 100 metros cuadrados costaba de media 900 euros, hoy son 1.525 euros. Al mismo tiempo, entre 2015 y 2025, según datos de la Administración de Estadística de Berlín, los ingresos per cápita en la ciudad habían aumentado un 33%, menos de la mitad de lo que se ha encarecido tener un hogar. El impacto social es mayúsculo porque se le añade que un 83% de los berlineses viven de alquiler . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Victor Glover, piloto de Artemis 2: “Llevaremos humanos a Marte y, para ello, ganaremos a China la carrera al polo sur de la Luna”
items.description: Hace cinco meses, cuatro chicas entusiasmadas entraron con su madre en una zona de máxima seguridad luciendo la misma camiseta negra, en la que iba estampada una foto de su padre. Unos minutos después, este salió de un edificio vigilado por el ejército, entre flashes y cámaras de televisión, y les miró con los ojos humedecidos desde el otro lado de la valla. No podía acercarse ni tocarlas. Tenía que respetar la cuarentena, porque en unas horas iba a subirse al cohete tripulado más potente de la historia y se iría a la Luna . Sin hablar, se decían todo, y el resto del mundo les entendía. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El alma no tiene pasaporte
items.description: Dice mi querida Shakira , releyendo al maestro Gabriel García Márquez en su precioso texto del pasado 31 de agosto , que la soledad no tiene por qué durar cien años. Para curar ese frío no basta con mirarnos al espejo: hay que ensanchar la casa, abrir las puertas de par en par, tirar los tabiques y darnos cuenta de que la mesa es mucho más grande de lo que nos habían contado. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Louis Dreyfus, presidente de ‘Le Monde’: “Nuestro modelo de negocio es la independencia”
items.description: Aquí no había nada en 2014. O, más bien, solo un agujero y un periódico que había pasado por un periodo de quiebra técnica. La sede del grupo Le Monde , terminada poco antes de la pandemia, está concebida como un edificio-puente de cristal. Una gran estructura arqueada que cruza sobre un espacio público y las vías ferroviarias junto a la estación de Austerlitz. Pero, sobre todo, como la declaración de intenciones en pleno centro de París de un periódico que logró reponerse a una parada cardíaca, reflotar su negocio y convertirse hoy en un artefacto empresarial controlado por una fundación y sus propios empleados. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El libro total
items.description: Eran dos hermanos colombianos, Álvaro y Gonzalo, y tuvieron un sueño. Me cuentan que se reunían cada sábado en la casa de Álvaro, el menor de ellos, y hablaban largo y tendido de lo humano y lo divino. Pero siempre había un tiempo para que conversaran de sus lecturas, de su pasión por los libros. Y en algún momento, sin imaginar aun lo que provocarían, hasta soñaron con lo útil y hermoso que sería entrar en una biblioteca en donde estuvieran al alcance de sus ojos muchos libros, incluso —solo era un sueño— en la que se almacenaran todos los libros, la sabiduría del mundo. Una biblioteca infinita o interminable como la que había anhelado Jorge Luis Borges y que hasta concibió para su relato La biblioteca de Babel. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Europa se atrinchera frente a la guerra híbrida de Rusia
items.description: Rusia intensifica su guerra híbrida contra Europa. Desde sabotajes, incursiones con drones e incendios provocados a complots (la mayoría, frustrados) para asesinar a activistas pro-Ucrania y disidentes rusos en suelo europeo. El Kremlin está poniendo a prueba la respuesta aliada, y los incidentes contra los aliados europeos de la OTAN son cada vez más serios. Como los drones con explosivos localizados este verano en el aeropuerto de Leipzig (Alemania). Esa línea gris entre un ataque híbrido y uno convencional se está difuminando, y varias fuentes de inteligencia europeas advierten del riesgo de que uno de esos incidentes escale. Por una decisión deliberada del Kremlin o por un error de cálculo, indican. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cómo Putin, Trump y Xi buscan que la UE fracase
items.description: Vladímir Putin se halla en dificultad. La guerra en Ucrania no le va bien, las bajas son una hemorragia impresionante, el malestar de la sociedad rusa crece en medio de serias dificultades económicas , la perplejidad de la corte del Kremlin ante la ineficacia del líder se intensifica. Su respuesta, de momento, está siendo la de siempre: una escalada. Contra Ucrania, con más misiles; contra su ciudadanía, con más represión; y contra la UE, con ataques, amenazas y provocaciones de distinto tipo ―sabotajes, ciber, incursiones―, cada vez más atrevidos y peligrosos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las obsesiones de Trump hunden a los republicanos en las encuestas de noviembre
items.description: Hay una frase en la neolengua trumpista que se usa para indicar que el presidente de Estados Unidos está encima de los asuntos, “enfocado [en ellos] con la precisión de un láser” . El problema a 38 días de las elecciones de mitad de mandato (las midterms ) es que las encuestas indican que los votantes no están conformes con los temas a los que Trump está apuntando con ese láser. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Crónica de una barra de pan en Ceuta: de la escasez a la radicalización
items.description: No es harina, agua, levadura y sal. Tampoco un símbolo. Desde que estalló la crisis migratoria en Ceuta, el pan se ha convertido en un síntoma, un termómetro de los casi dos meses que esta ciudad lleva viviendo en la excepción absoluta en casi todos los ámbitos posibles, y también algunos que parecían imposibles. Las barras de pan fueron lo primero en agotarse cuando entre el 30 y el 31 de julio cerca de 80.000 personas entraron en una ciudad que apretaba ya esa misma cifra de habitantes en apenas 20 kilómetros cuadrados. Se quedaron 10.000, pero el Ministerio del Interior insistió durante semanas en rebajar la cifra a algo más de 2.000, lo que fue fermentando buena parte de los conflictos que llegarían al horno después. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cuenta atrás para el regreso de Puigdemont: un plan guardado en un ordenador protegido
items.description: El bloqueo judicial de la ley de amnistía toca a su fin. La agenda del Tribunal Constitucional tiene marcado en rojo el martes 6 de octubre para dar el carpetazo definitivo al delito de malversación que sigue pesando sobre los líderes del procés . Es una trama con poco suspense porque la mayoría progresista del Constitucional ya ha avanzado que no pondrá objeciones al borrón y cuenta nueva. Tras larga espera , el despliegue de la amnistía cuenta ahora con dos bazas donde apoyarse: el recurso que presentó la exconsellera Dolors Bassa, cuya ponencia depende del presidente Cándido Conde-Pumpido, o el de Jordi Turull, pendiente del magistrado conservador José María Macías . Seguir leyendo

items.title: Adiós al polémico juez Peinado: ¿qué legado deja el instructor del ‘caso Begoña Gómez’?
items.description: El magistrado Juan Carlos Peinado cuelga la toga este domingo: cumple 72 años y, como marca la ley, ha alcanzado la edad máxima para seguir ejerciendo. El juez instructor, un desconocido cuando se hizo cargo del caso Begoña Gómez en abril de 2024, se marcha seis días después de mandar al banquillo por primera vez a la esposa de un presidente del Gobierno y convertido en una figura muy controvertida. Visto como un héroe por un sector de la derecha; como un “prevaricador” por el Ejecutivo y por las fuerzas de izquierdas; y criticado en público (y mucho más en privado) dentro de la propia carrera jurídica. Su chirriante investigación sobre la pareja del socialista Pedro Sánchez ya forma parte de la reciente historia de este país. Pero, ¿qué legado deja? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los secuestros, un código violento del mundo criminal
items.description: Que los coches rueden a 120 kilómetros por hora no intimida a los delincuentes. Dos vehículos se cruzan en la carretera y paran el tráfico de la AP-7. Llevan pasamontañas, unos chalecos reflectantes en los que se lee “Policía” y van directos a por su objetivo. Abren la puerta del copiloto y tiran hasta que arrancan al hombre del asiento del vehículo que conduce su novia. Se le ve con la cara ensangrentada, descalzo y la ropa rota, mientras le arrastran por el suelo hasta otro coche. Los demás conductores asisten atónitos a lo que ocurre un sábado a las siete y media de la tarde en la principal autopista de Cataluña. Algunos lo graban. Es un secuestro entre delincuentes, pero eso solo lo saben los protagonistas, los investigadores que ahora buscan a los autores y el entorno criminal. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Igor Yebra, estrella internacional de la danza: “Tengo esclerosis múltiple desde 2015″
items.description: “Siempre he sido muy reservado, mucho, y creo que uno de los motivos por los que me he abierto con este libro ha sido porque no quería ni podía sostener más esta enfermedad en secreto”. Habla el bailarín y coreógrafo vasco Igor Yebra (Bilbao, 54 años) desde Montevideo, donde ha viajado para organizar un concurso para fomentar la danza clásica entre niños y niñas. En Uruguay son las ocho y media de la mañana, pero él ya luce como si llevara despierto varias horas. Cuenta por videollamada que suele entrenar temprano y en los últimos años, más aún. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Pilar Castro, actriz: “He trabajado muy duro para no ser solo la rubia”
items.description: Quedamos a la una de la tarde en una librería-cafetería recién abierta en su barrio, en una zona a la vez residencial y populosa de Madrid. Llega apurada, con ligero retraso, vestida con vaqueros, sudadera y deportivas, con el pelo lavado de casa y un ligerísimo maquillaje, como quien se ha arreglado lo justo para salir a la calle. Tiene muchísima prisa. Se disculpa alegando que se ha dejado un puré de verduras haciéndose y debe de ser cierto porque, después de la apresurada sesión de fotos y de la apresurada conversación, que accede a completar otro día por teléfono, sale literalmente corriendo por la acera hasta perderse de vista. Hace menos de 24 horas, anoche, esta mujer rabiosamente contemporánea y urbanita, encarnaba a la marquesa de Merteuil, una madura aristócrata devastada con el rostro convulso por el despecho y el sufrimiento en el cuadro final de Las amistades peligrosas, la obra teatral que representa estos días en Madrid. Seguir leyendo FURIA Y CALMA Pilar Castro (Madrid, 55 años) siempre quiso ser artista. Trabajó como bailarina en el mítico programa de TVE Aplauso antes de estudiar interpretación en la escuela de Cristina Rota y debutar en el cine en Historias del Kronen , en 1995. Después, paralelamente a sus papeles en montajes de la compañía Animalario, y de la suya propia, Caracalva, con Secun de la Rosa, formó parte del reparto de la exitosa saga Los dos lados de la cama y otros títulos que forman parte de la memoria sentimental de su generación. Su último papel, después de protagonizar uno de los capítulos de la serie Furia , es el de la marquesa de Merteuil en Las amistades peligrosas , junto a Roberto Enríquez, dirigidos por David Serrano, en cartel estos días en Madrid antes de salir de gira por toda España.

items.title: Qué pena que no vayan a leer a Lena Dunham
items.description: Es una pena que buena parte de los fans de Lena Dunham se vayan a perder Famesick , su prodigioso libro de memorias sobre la fama y la enfermedad que acaba de editarse en España. Es lastimoso que una sentencia moral rotunda —que puedo compartir— les prive de una lectura tan inteligente, divertida, profunda y ligera a la vez. Supongo que es el sino del personaje, condenado desde siempre a ser amado y odiado con la misma ferocidad, por las mismas personas y, a menudo, por las mismas razones. Quien se enamoró de su frivolidad de niña pija en Girls la detestó por ser una niña pija frívola. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Of William Ruto's big talk at UNGA with small action at home
Así negocia el Gobierno el decreto antidesahucios
El negocio de perseguir a la hija de Zapatero
items.description: Una joven anda apresurada por la calle con un perrito debajo del brazo y un tipo, micrófono en mano, la acosa con comentarios del tipo “¿por qué cobrabais en negro? No me digas que porque sois góticas porque no cuela”, “¿no te da vergüenza?”, “¿crees que vas a acabar en la cárcel como tu padre?” o “dale de comer al perro, que está muy delgado”. La chica es Laura Rodríguez Espinosa, hija del expresidente José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, a quien solo se le oye repetir “no me persigas” mientras aligera el paso para intentar, sin éxito, zafarse de Vito Quiles. Hasta esta semana, el agitador ultra tenía acreditación en el Congreso . La mantiene en el Senado después de haber participado en actos del Partido Popular, que se opuso junto a Vox a la normativa por la que se le ha sancionado y expulsado de la Cámara baja. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Somalia, el país que entierra a bebés muertos de hambre: “Ya solo confiamos en la ayuda de Dios”
items.description: Shukri Mahad Mohamed tiene cuatro años. Pesa cuatro kilos y medio. Eso supone unas cuatro veces menos de lo que debería pesar. Su figura esquelética se pierde entre el tejido que lo mantiene envuelto en el regazo de su madre. En riguroso silencio, sobre una silla de plástico, Madina Osman Hassan, de 22 años, observa el rostro consumido de su hijo en el Hospital Daynile de Mogadiscio, capital de Somalia , primer país donde, en 2011, se decretó una hambruna en el siglo XXI. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los fundadores de On, el fenómeno que atrae a Mbappé y Zendaya: “El coste no es un factor limitante; nuestros seguidores están dispuestos a pagar”
items.description: Quizá se haya cruzado últimamente con alguna de estas zapatillas deportivas con inquietantes agujeros en la suela. Si se ha fijado, es posible que ya haya visto muchas. No es una sensación suya, es que en pocos años los diseños de la marca On se han expandido por todo el globo. Fuera del terreno deportivo, la etiqueta era una desconocida antes de la pandemia, pero ahora se ha convertido en un fenómeno cultural que trasciende el universo del running. Su último golpe de efecto lo dio la semana pasada, cuando anunció que había sellado un acuerdo con el delantero del Real Madrid Kylian Mbappé, que abandonaba Nike tras 20 años de colaboración. Además, On ya colabora regularmente con la firma de lujo Loewe, con la superestrella Zendaya o con el extenista Roger Federer. A este último le sedujo tanto la firma que se convirtió en uno de sus accionistas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tracking Senator Benson Agadaga’s 10th Assembly record
items.description: By Wole Adeshina In the chambers of the 10th Senate, legislative representation is measured by concrete outputs: bills sponsored, motions raised, and physical development brought directly to constituents. On these metrics, Senator Benson Agadaga has established himself as one of the most active lawmakers representing the South-South region. Key Sponsored Bills and Motions Border Communities Development Agency (BCDA) Act Amendment Bill: Sponsored an amendment bill to alter the provisions of the BCDA Act (2006) to insert additional neglected maritime border communities across Bayelsa East into federal development frameworks. items.title: Miners death probe: Commend President Tinubu for empowering Interior Minister
items.description: By Saka Ola Ahmed The death of 37 suspected illegal miners while in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, in Minna, Niger State has thrown the nation into grief. Outrage has rightly been expressed by Nigerians who called for an urgent probe of the unfortunate incident. Recall 37 out of 65 detained suspects died under disputed circumstances in an NSCDC facility in Minna following their arrests on September 15 and 16, 2026.Survivors alleged suffocation from overcrowding and a chemical substance sprayed in the cell. The Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo immediately visited Minna, Niger State, following the tragic incident and met with Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago at the Government House in Minna to inspect and address the situation, vowing that the deaths would “not be swept under the carpet”. The federal government took immediate action by suspending the Niger State NSCDC Commandant along with 20 other officers. Governor Bago also announced a total suspension of all mining activities, both legal and illegal, across Niger State pending safety tests. President Bola Tinubu must be commended for empowering the Interior Minister to take control and probe the immediate and remote cause or causes of the unfortunate death of the miners, most of who were teenagers. The President is currently on vacation in Europe and has been monitoring events while giving the Interior Minister free hand to handle the investigation of the incident. There is a general belief that you cannot give an important message to someone to deliver if you know that person will not be able to deliver the message. Giving Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo the task of unravelling what actually happened is a mark of the confidence the President has on the ability of the Minister to do the job diligently and dispassionately. An investigative committee has already been inaugurated by the Minister to ensure full accountability and transparency regarding the cause of death. On Tuesday, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo inaugurated a 10-member Independent Investigative Committee to probe the death of the 37 suspected illegal miners. While inaugurating the panel in Abuja, he declared that government institutions must never become places of death, assuring Nigerians that no officer found culpable would be shielded. “No life should be lost in the custody of the State. This is not who we are. This is not what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu stands for. “This administration was elected on the premise that every Nigerian life matters and that security must be provided with humanity, professionalism, and respect for human rights,” he said. The minister has expressed condolences to the families of the deceased, the government and people of Niger State, and other Nigerians affected by the incident, describing it as one of the lowest moments in recent memory. He revealed that following President Tinubu’s directive for a comprehensive, transparent and unhindered investigation, he ordered the immediate suspension of the Niger State Commandant of the NSCDC and the arrest and investigation of all officers who were on guard duties between September 15 and 17. “They remain suspended pending the outcome of this investigation,” he said. According to the minister, the committee is expected to establish the identities of the deceased and document the circumstances surrounding their arrest and detention. It will also determine, through appropriate medical and forensic examinations, the cause and manner of death, as well as investigate whether negligence, misconduct, complicity or any breach of duty occurred. The panel is further expected to recommend appropriate disciplinary measures, compensation where applicable and steps to prevent a recurrence. Tunji-Ojo named retired Deputy Director-General of the Department of State Services, Jonathan Kure, as chairman of the committee, while a former Director-General of the Nigeria Law School, Prof. Isa Hayatu Chiroma, will serve as secretary. The minister has also said the committee had full authority to co-opt experts, access facilities and documents, visit relevant locations, conduct forensic examinations, and receive memoranda from members of the public. He gave the panel two weeks to complete its assignment and submit its report. From the above meticulous terms of reference given to the panel, one can expect a thorough job and good report from the panel. As is characteristic of the Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, he will follow through the recommendations of the panel and ensure that such sad incident does not occur again. The post Miners death probe: Commend President Tinubu for empowering Interior Minister appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The season of mercy, by Funmi Komolafe
items.description: Beloved, as we progress into the ember months, may God show us mercy in Jesus name. For a Christian, the ember months are not to be feared. Rather, it should be seen as the months of mercy. Why? It is because it is time for all prayers to be answered. Indeed a season of testimony. The ember months should be seen, as the months of that should actualize our dreams, goals of visions. Note that the word Remember ends with ember so, it is time for God to remember you and when God remembers a person that person will surely benefit from his mercy Beloved, if indeed, you have been praying for a miracle in a particular area since the beginning of the year and that miracle is yet to manifest, it is time to ask for mercy. Why do you need to ask for mercy? It could be that you have not been praying with a focus, or you might have hindered the miracle by your own action. It could even be as a result of enemies using monitoring spirits to work against your God given miracle. What ever is the reason for the delay, God can show mercy. Let’s consider the conversation of Daniel with an angel of God. Daniel 10 vs. 11-14 (NIV) : He said, “ Daniel, you who are highly esteemed, consider carefully the words I am about to speak to you, and stand up, for I have been sent to you”. And when he said this to me, I stood up trembling. Then he continued, Do not be afraid. Daniel. Since the first day that you set your mind to gain understanding and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come in response to them. But the prince of the Persian kingdom resisted me twenty one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me because I was detained there with the king of Persia. Now I have come to explain to you what will happen to your people in the future, for the vision concerns a time yet to come”. Here the Bible mentions that Daniel was humble in his prayer. He prayed asking for mercy. His prayers were not about entitlement. God heard but a monitoring spirit hindered the manifestation of his testimony. Are going through a similar condition? Have been fasting and praying without testimonies to show for it? If confronted with a situation like this, you don’t need to war like prayers. Why? It is because; God has seen the number of monitoring spirits that you haven’t seen that have hindered your prayer. In a situation like this, you need God’s mercy for the prayers to be answered. Note that the angel told Daniel that the “ vision concerns a time yet to come”. Brethren, it is up to you if you want the vision to manifest now or for a time yet to come. Many are likely to desire instant manifestation of the vision. Therefor your prayer is found in Psalm 102 vs. 13: “ You will arise and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to show favour to her, the appointed time has come”. You may need to put your name in place of Zion and me to replace her. This is not a one off prayer but one that must be consistently and regularly prayed for the answer to come. Beloved, when praying, we need to be specific. Assume you are in a conversation with a personality while praying and state clearly what you want from the LORD. The situation of Abraham and Sarah is similar to what some couples are going thorough. Many have asked, why the long delay after a dedication of life and service to God, praying and fasting? It is natural to ask such questions but may you receive the mercy of God this season that you may testify to a miracle in Jesus name. Abraham and Sarah kindly treated strangers not knowing that they had entertained God in human flesh. What did they get in return? Genesis 18 vs. 9&10 ( KJV) tells us more. “ And they said unto him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent. And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent, which was behind him”. Sarah had doubts because of her age but Beloved , when dealing with God, age isn’t a barrie The couple showered the strangers with mercy and they received great mercy. Genesis 21 vs. 1-3 completes the story. It states, “ And the LORD visited Sarah as he had said, and the LORD did unto Sarah as he had spoken. For Sarah conceived, and bare Abraham a son in his old age, at the set time of which God had spoken to him. And Abraham called the name of his son that was born unto him, whom Sarah bare to him, Isaac”. Perhaps you have been humiliated like Hannah. There is no need fighting or holding it against anyone. Just cry unto the LORD like Hannah and watch the LORD’s mercy show up in your life. Hannah shunned Peninnah’s provocation. Rather than engage in unnecessary altercations, she went to the LORD in prayer. The Holy Bible puts it this way in 1st Samuel 1 vs. 10 ( KJV) “ And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the LORD, and wept sore”. The mockery of Peninnah made her to take her prayer more seriously. She wept and prayed. When last did tears drop from your eyes while praying? It isn’t a condition for a miracle but it is an evidence of someone who is pouring our her mind to the Almighty God. Hannah’s determination to have an answer to her prayer made her make a vow. 1st Samuel 10 vs. 11: “ And she vowed a vow, and said, O LORD of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the LORD all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head”. Beloved, be determined to get your miracle before the year ends by asking for the mercy of God. 2025 is running out but with the mercy of God, it would not run away with your miracle in Jesus name. Remember, His mercy endureth forever. Shalom ! The post The season of mercy, by Funmi Komolafe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Houthi blockade
items.description: IN July 2026, the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia, targeting Saudi-linked shipping, and warning commercial vessels of any nationality against calling at Saudi ports. Vessels deemed to breach the blockade faced attack wherever they entered the Houthis’ operational reach. Attacks on Saudi tankers and energy infrastructure were followed by traffic through Bab al-Mandeb falling to its lowest level in months. By September, Houthi forces had seized strategic islands around Bab al-Mandeb and gained control of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, increasing their capacity to threaten, disrupt and potentially control maritime traffic through the strait. The conventional legal position is that naval blockade is a belligerent right associated with international armed conflict (IAC), mainly because it permits interference with neutral commercial shipping. As per this view, a non-state armed group engaged solely in a non-international armed conflict does not ordinarily have the authority to impose a blockade that is binding on neutral vessels. However, customary international law does not conclusively foreclose blockade in a sufficiently intense NIAC, particularly where an organised armed group exercises extensive territorial and governmental control and can enforce maritime restrictions. This question is particularly significant in Yemen, where there is a strong argument that the Houthis function as a de facto governmental authority rather than merely an insurgent movement. They have long controlled Sana’a, govern territory containing a substantial population, and have expanded along the Red Sea coast and around Bab al-Mandeb. Crucially, under the ICRC approach, effective governmental control, rather than global recognition alone, is central to determining de facto governmental authority. If the Houthis are treated as exercising Yemen’s governmental authority, their external hostilities may be characterised as those of Yemen itself, strengthening the argument that the relevant conflicts are international and that traditional belligerent rights, including blockade, are potentially available. Even if this characterisation is rejected, other factors point towards possible internationalisation. Saudi Arabia is directly engaged alongside the internationally recognised Yemeni authorities against the Houthis, while the latter have repeatedly attacked Saudi territory. Saudi intervention by invitation does not, by itself, transform the underlying conflict into an IAC, but it adds an international dimension. Israel provides a separate route: it has used force on Yemeni territory in response to Houthi attacks, and under the ICRC’s view, the unconsented use of force by one state against another state’s territory may itself create an IAC between them, even where the immediate target is a non-state armed group. Israeli strikes on Houthi-held territory could therefore support a parallel Israel-Yemen IAC. Do the Houthis, as a non-state armed group, have the legal authority to enforce a naval blockade? Iranian involvement provides another possible route to internationalisation. Arms, financing and political support alone are insufficient. Under the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia’s “overall control” test in Tadić, however, the threshold may be met where a state, beyond financing, training or equipping an organised armed group, also participates in planning its military activities; specific instructions for each operation are unnecessary. The ICJ’s stricter “effective control” test, relevant to attribution of particular conduct, requires proof that the state directed or controlled the specific operation in question. Accordingly, if the conflict is international, traditional blockade law is more readily applicable; if the Houthis remain solely a non-state party to an NIAC, their authority to impose blockade obligations on neutral shipping remains controversial. In either case, a declaration alone is insufficient: a blockade must satisfy the requirements of effectiveness, notification, impartiality and applicable humanitarian limitations. Regardless of classification, the Houthis are bound by applicable international humanitarian law. In an NIAC, Common Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions and applicable customary IHL apply; in an IAC, the Geneva Conventions apply in full, together with customary IHL. In either case, rules governing distinction, military goals, proportionality and precautions constrain the conduct of hostilities. The law of naval blockade is further governed by the law of armed conflict at sea and customary international law, as elaborated in the San Remo Manual. Under paragraphs 93-104, a blockade must be declared and notified to belligerents and neutral states; specify its commencement, duration, location and extent; allow neutral vessels an appropriate period to depart; be effective and impartially applied; and comply with humanitarian restrictions, including those concerning essential civilian supplies. Importantly, the Houthis have denied seeking to close Bab al-Mandeb to international navigation. Their spokesman stated that there was “no closure” of the strait and described the measure as a maritime blockade affecting only the Saudi side. The main legal question, therefore, is not whether the Houthis may close Bab al-Mandeb as a coastal authority, but whether they may lawfully impose and enforce a belligerent blockade against Saudi Arabia and shipping falling within its scope. Military necessity, however, does not independently make commercial shipping a lawful target. Article 52(2) of Additional Protocol I, reflecting the customary definition of a military objective, requires an object, by its nature, location, purpose or use, to make an effective contribution to military action and for its destruction, capture or neutralisation to offer a definite military advantage. Particular Saudi vessels, ports or assets directly supporting military operations may satisfy that test, but the general contribution of commercial trade to Saudi Arabia’s economy and war capacity does not, by itself, transform every merchant vessel into a military goal. Any attack remains subject to distinction, proportionality and precautions. This distinction is particularly important for neutral shipping. Neutral vessels do not lose protection merely because they trade with Saudi Arabia or indirectly contribute to its economy. Whether a vessel may lawfully be intercepted, cap­­tured or attacked must be determined under the specific rules governing blockade, neutral shipping and military objectives, rather than through a general invocation of military necessity. Finally, the simultaneous closure of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb would place roughly a quarter of global oil flows and a major share of LNG trade at risk. Some analysts view pressure on both chokepoints as part of a broader Iranian strategy, working through the Houthis to increase economic pressure on the US and its Gulf partners and create leverage over the wider war. Pakistan has condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia while continuing to stress diplomacy and regional de-escalation. It has so far avoided direct military involvement under the Makkah accord, maintaining a cautious approach that limits the risk of Pakistan being drawn into the widening regional conflict. The writer is a professor of law at Lums. Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026

items.title: How Niger Delta was underdeveloped by its leaders, by Dele Sobowale
items.description: “Niger Delta got $160bn in 27 yrs, yet remains underdeveloped – Aig-Imoukhuede ” – VANGUARD, SEPTEMBER 16, 2026. “Every country has the government it deserves” – Joseph de Maistre, 1753-1821. Thank God for Nigerians like Aig-Imoukhuede who occasionally seizes the opportunity to tell Nigerians the truth we hate to hear. He was the Keynote Address Speaker at the Niger Delta Economic and Investment Summit 2026 held in Port Harcourt. The Summit itself is symptomatic of the way billions of naira is wasted by the leaders of the Niger Delta. Delta State had its own Economic Summit a few weeks before. Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala was in attendance to proffer advice which will be soundly applauded and routinely disregarded by the governors. Nobody should expect anything meaningful after the two summits. Just as every country deserves the government it has, every sub-national region is the architect of its own fortune or misfortune. To start with, $160bn exceeds the national debt by far. At N1,400/$US1, N224trn has been collected by the governments since 1999 – with very little development to show for it. That was the message Aig-Imoukhuede was trying to get across. BETRAYAL OF ATTAH’S FIGHT FOR RESOURCE CONTROL “The traitors in our midst, always highly trusted, always splendid fellows, always the last people to be suspected” – Agatha Christie, 1890-1976 That was centuries ago. Right now, the traitors of the Niger Delta people, with one exception, Obong Victor Attah, cannot often be described as splendid fellows; and few people trust them. They are the leaders of the region. When Attah led the struggle for RESOURCE CONTROL, as governor of Akwa Ibom State, he envisaged that receiving well-deserved higher percentage of derivation would lead to more rapid development of the region. He succeeded in getting more money for his people, and I can state authoritatively that Attah is an extremely unhappy man today. Niger Delta, today, is so far behind, in terms of development, that those familiar with the region would be forgiven for wondering if it will ever become developed. The rot set in very early. FROM 1999 TO 2026 “A nation of sheep will soon have a government of wolves” – Anonymous The nine states constituting the Niger Delta, before the recent inclusion of Anambra State – are ancestral homes to several nation-states. Igbo, Ijaw, Urhobo, Ibibio, Bini, Itsekiri, Ilaje, Efik, Anang, to name a few. They were all colonized by the British and suffered the consequences of subjugation; like the rest of Nigeria. Independence ostensibly came in 1960 giving the people a chance to become masters of their own fates. That dream was short-lived when wolves in uniform seized power; relinquished it for four years; and took it again for 16 years. The colonial officers posted to Nigeria retired to stupendous wealth; the Nigerian satraps who controlled power and resources also retired to astonishing wealth by 1999. Naively, civilian Nigerians assumed that the Fourth Republic would be different. We were wrong. The ruling party, Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, started by the G-34 and led by the late Dr Alex Ekwueme, was hijacked by the military. Retired General Obasanjo was imposed on Nigerians; and, unknown to us, the reign of wolves continued. What happened in some states of the Niger Delta was replicated in several states of Nigeria. One South-West state was badly hit. Civilian governors proceeded to establish opulent life-styles – which the worst colonial officer could not have imagined – irrespective of the party. However, since the region under review is the Niger Delta – which included states from the South-East, South-South and South-West, this article will focus on that region; especially when a concerned son has asked a vital question – which needs to be answered urgently as the people of the region have another chance to liberate themselves from underserved perpetual backwardness and under-development. Most Niger Deltans might not remember, and some might not care, but some of the nine governors in the Class of 1999-2007 were eventually charged with embezzlement of public funds. Some of the second and third generations of governors were not much better. When the All Progressives Congress, APC, took power in 2015, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, former Edo State governor and then-party leader, had announced openly: “Join the APC and your sins are forgiven”. Today, four former governors and some APC members have their files gathering dust in EFCC’s office. How did these happen? POLITICIANS, COURTS AND EFCC Politicians, the courts and the EFCC have colluded to bring this situation about. Unfortunately, space constraints will not allow me to elaborate. But let me leave you with an astonishing true story from the past. ALAMIEYESEIGHA FACES 39-COUNT CHARGE – VANGUARD, December 21, 2005 Below, without any elaboration for now, are the first 33 charges and the amounts involved. The remaining six will be dealt with in the second volume of this series. 1. N1.5 billion converted to buy Chelsea Hotel, Abuja. 2. N450 million to buy property on Plot 26, Bashir Dalhatu Close, Abacha Estate, Ikoyi. 3. N435 million to buy property at John Kadiya Close, Asokoro, Abuja. 4. N420 million to buy properties at 1, Community Road, off Allen Avenue, Ikeja. 5. N1 billion to buy shares in Bond Bank, Lagos. 6. Three million pounds transfer from Lagos to Barclays Bank Plc London. 7. One hundred thousand pounds transfer from Lagos to the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 8. Seventy million pounds transfer from Lagos to the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 9. Fifty million pounds transfer from Lagos to the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 10. One hundred and twenty two thousand pounds transfer to the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 11. Seventy thousand pounds transfer to the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 12. One hundred and ninety eight thousand pounds transfer to the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 13. One hundred and twenty thousand pounds transfer to the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 14. One hundred thousand pounds transfer to Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 15. $250,000 transfer from Lagos to the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 16. Almost one hundred thousand pounds transfer to the National Westminster Bank, London, a subsidiary of the Royal Bank of Scotland, London. 17. Almost eighty two thousand pounds transfer to National Westminster Bank of London 18. Almost twenty thousand pounds transfer to National Westminster Bank. 19. One hundred and thirty-six thousand pounds transfer to the National Westminster Bank. 20. Two hundred and seventy-five pounds transfer to the National Westminster Bank. 21. Two hundred and ninety-nine pounds to the National Westminster Bank. 22. Two hundred and four thousand pounds transfer to Barclays Bank Plc of London. 23. 175 million pounds transfer to London to purchase property. 24. 1.4 million pounds transfer to buy London property. 25. Converted 241 million pounds to buy London property 26. Converted 3 million pounds to buy property in London 27. Converted almost 476, 000 pounds to buy property in London. 28. Converted $409,761.24 to buy property in London. 29. Converted 1 million pounds to buy property in South Africa. 30. Converted N250 million to buy property at Ikoyi. 31. Transferred $160,000 to open account in US. 32. Transferred N35 million to Port Harcourt to buy property. 33. Had N105 million balances in personal account No 2010062850006 at Bond Bank Plc. In my book, ‘PDP: CORRUPTION INCORPORATED’, pages 269-270, these properties were estimated to be worth about N220 billion by 2009. Alamieyeseigha was not initially arrested in Nigeria; he was apprehended in the UK; charged to court and granted bail. He jumped bail; returned to Nigeria and a hero’s welcome in Bayelsa State. Need more evidence why Niger Delta is still undeveloped? There is more. Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola. items.title: How many men after 30 years of marriage still love their wives?
items.description: By Bunmi Sofola MEN are the strongest allies when protecting their philandering interests. Alex, an industrialist in his 60s recognized his first son’s potential as a businessman when he made brilliant success of his secondary school exams. Getting him a place in one of the universities abroad was a doddle. As soon as he finished his masters degree in business admin., Alex asked Francis, his son, to join the firm. “I was very happy to,” Francis said “as I’d helped several times when I was on vacation. “I was 25, the whole world at my feet when dad put me in charge of production, a department I’d always worked with from time to time. We were a family of six children and dad worshipped the earth mum walked on. A close knit family, we always shared each other’s success and pain. The day all this changed, I was in dad’s office, discussing very thorny problems when he left me to things and hurried to an appointment he had earlier. Still engrossed in figures, I absent-mindedly picked up the phone when it rang and a female voice purred: ‘Hello darling workaholic. When are you showing your face here? Betty is anxious to show off the things you brought back for her from your last trip.’ ‘Excuse me’, I said, confused, ‘who exactly are you?’ Oh, ‘I’m sorry’, said this cultured voice, ‘thought the MD was still in his office. Could you tell him, Sola, his wife called?’ She then rang off. She obviously thought I was an ordinary member of staff. “I felt as if someone had hit me in the stomach. Of course, I guessed straight away that, Sola, the ‘wife’ was my dad’s mistress. But who was Betty? It took a lot of diplomacy to find out that most members of staff knew Sola as my dad’s second ‘wife’ and Betty was their daughter. That was when I realized a serpent had entered the garden of Eden my family lived in. Poor mum, she had left a promising nursing career to raise us kids. How could dad do this to her? To us? Over the years, he’d drummed it into his children how important it was to be above board and to be fair in how we deal with other human beings. Definitely, deceit was a sin as far as he knew. So where do we all go from here? I’m petrified thinking of confronting dad, not to talk of putting mum and my siblings in the picture. It would destroy the happy family we now take for granted …? I told Francis I would give his problem a thought. Then it occurred to me that I shouldn’t give the answers all of the time so I asked a few people. Yemisi, a married mother of three was the first to voice her opinion. She told me: “My first word which goes to the ‘baby’ graduate “is, he ain’t seen nothing yet! I find it difficult to believe we still have such a perfect gentleman like his father in Nigeria.” “Apart from being a successful businessman, he caters well enough for his number one family and still loves his wife after almost thirty years of marriage. For this alone, he deserves the ‘Best father of the century’ award. He again tries as much as possible to keep his affairs from his family. This I believe he does not intend to keep from at least his first son for too long. If not he would not, have asked him to work for him knowing very well that his mistress visits his office that often. “I think this man is a father in a million. Though it is bad enough that he has a child outside his matrimonial home, but then let us search our minds and see. How many fathers have such affairs and still keep a happy home? How many men after thirty years of marriage still respect and love their wives that much? Not very many men have we known to deny such a story to a son they educated, clothed and fed. “If we all compare our family lives with this man’s (I don’t mean the newly married or those who are five years old in the biz) we would realize that this gentleman deserves an applause from us all. His advising his children to behave decently does not make him a hypocrite, after all, experience they say is the best teacher. So, I consider this man who has been in this type of mess the right person to advise the young ones. “To the big ‘baby’, I say grow up – and talk more to your old man about his ‘problem’. He needs your advice as much as you need his. I also wish you to write and publish your own love story after 30 years of marriage. In the meantime, you should let a sleeping dog lie. When the time comes, you will be the one to tell and also give your old woman the heart to bear the shock of a supposed betrayal…” Justice’s male view is typical. He is 46 and a lecturer. According to him it is not a sin to get involved with another woman and rent a house for her while one is having an already well-established married home, provided one has the money. Polygamy is an indispensable African custom which we inherited from our ancestors. In the traditional society, a big man such as Alex is supposed to have not less than 20 wives. Polygamy is an inherited African cultural institution and it must continue to progress despite modern civilized habits and religious propaganda. “The fact that he advised his children to observe strict religious principles and run away from immoral and a scandalous behaviour does not mean that he himself is innocent. He wanted his children to live up to standard and have a promising future. “In my opinion, I would strongly advise the son not to tell his mother, but to try and be very friendly and intimate with Sola and his father, helping them sometimes to iron out their differences. The son would be termed absurd and unreasonable, if he instantly hates his father and Sola because of this. He will be a prodigal son, if he tells his mother. He must follow this advice, because he himself does not know which girls he would end up with in his search for marital bliss.” The post How many men after 30 years of marriage still love their wives? appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ateliers et colloques au menu du 31è FCMT
items.description: Le Festival de Cinéma Méditerranéen de Tétouan (FCMT), prévu du 3 au 10 octobre, poursuit son engagement en faveur de la création, de la réflexion et de la coopération méditerranéenne, en consacrant une partie de sa programmation à la transmission, aux échanges professionnels et aux enjeux qui traversent aujourd’hui le cinéma en Méditerranée. Selon un communiqué des organisateurs, cette 31e édition proposera, au-delà des projections et des compétitions, les Ateliers de Tétouan, deux colloques ainsi qu’un programme de coopération avec la ville italienne de Matera, réunissant cinéastes, producteurs, auteurs, chercheurs et jeunes talents autour de plusieurs temps de travail et de réflexion. Les Ateliers de Tétouan, l’un des programmes phares du festival, en sont à leur 4e édition. Ce fonds est dédié au développement de scripts de projets cinématographiques en cours d’écriture et vise à soutenir l’émergence de nouvelles voix du cinéma méditerranéen. Cette édition, indique le communiqué, réunira dix projets portés par onze cinéastes originaires de Turquie, de Syrie, du Liban, de Tunisie, de France et du Maroc, entre documentaire et fiction. Les projets documentaires sont portés par Otman Salil et Julia Le Noël, coréalisateurs, ainsi que Faïçal Benaghrou, Zineb Chafchaouni Moussouaoui et Ghina Daou. Les projets de fiction sont portés par Beril Tan, Lina Arious, Oussama Oussous, Reda Lahmouid, Yassine El Idrissi et Siba Younes. Les projets sélectionnés seront présentés devant un jury composé de Karim Aitouna, producteur au Maroc et en France, Mohamed Reda, journaliste senior en Angleterre, Bachir Edkhil, écrivain et analyste politique marocain, ainsi que Pilar Saavedra Perrotta, actrice et productrice italienne. Les Ateliers offrent aux porteurs de projets sélectionnés un soutien financier dédié au développement de l’écriture, ainsi qu’un cadre de travail consacré à la préparation du pitch et aux échanges avec des professionnels du secteur cinématographique. La rubrique Talents en Court proposera, pour sa part, une formation de trois jours spécialement dédiée aux étudiants de différentes écoles de cinéma et d’art au Maroc. Cette formation leur permettra d’explorer les différentes étapes de création d’un court métrage, de l’écriture du scénario à la réalisation, à travers des ateliers pratiques, des échanges d’expériences et des rencontres avec des professionnels du cinéma. Le programme sera coordonné par les cinéastes Mohamed Chrif Tribak et Nasser Abdelrahman. Le festival proposera également deux espaces de réflexion consacrés aux transformations qui touchent la création cinématographique et sa relation au public. Le premier colloque, intitulé Les nouvelles économies du cinéma en Méditerranée, interrogera les évolutions des modèles de production, de financement et de diffusion face aux mutations technologiques et économiques du secteur. Coproductions, circulation des œuvres, plateformes numériques, marchés nationaux et coopération entre les deux rives de la Méditerranée feront partie des sujets abordés. Cette rencontre réunira notamment Saïd Hamich, Hala Lotfy, Peter Marcias et Caroline Locardi Laraki, sous la modération de Khalid Zaïri, indique-t-on. Le deuxième colloque, Films-cinémas : enjeux de réception, s’intéressera au rapport entre les films et leurs spectateurs, à la mémoire cinématographique et à la place que les images occupent dans les récits personnels et collectifs. Il réunira la poétesse et scénariste Soukaina Habiballah, l’écrivain Abdelkader Chaoui, le poète et critique d’art Hassan Najmi et l’écrivain et philosophe Abderrahim Zaid. La rencontre sera modérée par Zohra Lhioui. Cette édition accueillera également une carte blanche au Matera Film Festival, dans le cadre de la coopération entre Tétouan et Matera et de l’initiative Matera, Capitale méditerranéenne de la culture et du dialogue 2026. En collaboration avec Cinecittà, et avec le soutien de plusieurs institutions italiennes, ce programme réunira des professionnels marocains et italiens autour des perspectives de coopération culturelle et cinématographique entre les deux pays. Une conférence institutionnelle présentera notamment les initiatives développées à Matera en 2026, tandis qu’un panel intitulé Producteurs italiens et marocains : nouvelles perspectives de coproduction abordera les possibilités de production, de coproduction, de distribution et de développement de projets. La rencontre accueillera notamment le producteur italien Mario Mazzarotto, aux côtés de professionnels marocains. Le public pourra par ailleurs découvrir une sélection de quatre films du Matera Film Festival, en présence d’une délégation italienne. Cette coopération se poursuivra en novembre 2026 à Matera, où une délégation du Festival de Tétouan participera à plusieurs activités aux côtés de personnalités du cinéma marocain. À travers ces différents programmes, le Festival de Cinéma Méditerranéen de Tétouan fait de la transmission, de la réflexion et de la coopération entre les cinématographies méditerranéennes trois axes importants de cette 31e édition. The post Ateliers et colloques au menu du 31è FCMT appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: A broken power accord
items.description: ALTHOUGH the PTI has postponed its protest march on Islamabad, the capital city’s container-blocked roads continue to reflect the country’s deeper crisis. The crisis is not merely political, economic, or security-related; it is rooted in an elite class that cannot forge an accord within themselves. Islamabad is not witnessing a siege-like situation for the first time; it has become part of life for the inhabitants of the twin cities. Even a cricket match or a visiting dignitary can bring life to a standstill. Despite huge investments in infrastructure and expensive surveillance systems, the security providers remain nervous. They have turned the federal capital into a city of checkpoints, where the average citizen must pass through long queues every 10 minutes during his daily commute — with police officers regarding him with suspicious eyes. Citizens end up feeling that they themselves are responsible for all the country’s ills, while those who have actually encroached on green belts, footpaths, and even highways escape punishment for crimes they do not even understand. The crisis runs deep, and even the postponement of the protest by the PTI, and earlier by the Jamaat-i-Islami , will not solve the country’s political, governance, economic, and security crisis. These lines may seem cynical, but the streets of the federal capital tell Pakistan’s whole story. The ‘container-ment’ approach shows serious fractures among the power elites over the division of power, which has not been shared proportionately and has, in fact, caused a chronic political crisis and led to a rent-seeking economy. Rent-seeking means economic actors become adept at obtaining privileged access to the state or controlling scarce resources. The masses are not responsible for the country’s state of affairs; it is fractured power elites who have yet to learn the art of distributing power among themselves. Here, another term needs explaining. The ‘fractured elite’ comprises Pakistan’s dominant political, civil-military, judicial, and institutional elite — sometimes referred to as the establishment — when it no longer agrees on the basic rules of the political game. The elite includes religious and ideological authorities, but in an evolving power order, their role and share have been minimised for now. Major businesses and landed interests have become important actors within the fractured power order. Serious fractures exist among the elites over the division of power. A question arises: what does an elite power accord look like? Is it about who will have the political power to govern, and under what conditions? Another question emerges: aside from political power, who holds the real power, also referred to as institutional power? Does this authority belong to parliament, the executive, the military, the judiciary, or the bureaucracy? Institutional power brings control over major economic resources and rents, as well as coercive or security institutions. It also has territorial power to determine how the interests of the centre and the provinces are accommodated. Among the elites, succession remains a key question: how will power change hands? A linked challenge arises. How are influential groups accommodated? Foreign policy remains the exclusive domain of the power elites — what strategic interests are considered non-negotiable? Now look at the Pakistani elites, which have failed to define the role of political power. Gradually, an institution has assumed authority, while the ruling political parties have surrendered several rights to retain power. The opposition, meanwhile, is demanding its legitimate rights. Many political analysts arguably contend that the opposition, now led by the PTI, along with smaller parties within the opposition alliance, the Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz-i-Ayeen-i-Pakistan, is struggling for power rather than restoring or developing a new social contract in the country. Maulana Fazlur Rahman’s JUI-F is also part of the opposition. It has been marginalised in the power structure because the changing rules in the power playbook leave less space for religious actors now. The political power structure has clearly failed to advance nationhood, and power remains confined to one major influential ethnic group in the country. Those who represent the power structure in the public discourse and the social and mainstream media malign less powerful and marginalised groups, suggesting they go to Afghanistan — their remarks target both the Pakhtuns and the Baloch. They stigmatise the Kashmiris as well, who have been demanding their rights in Azad Kashmir. If state propagandists are suggesting a course of action for them, where are they supposed to go? Fractured power elites cannot create cohesion within a nation. They cannot resolve their internal discord, so how can they devise a broad formula for national cohesion? In their paranoid view, security has taken over dialogue, and they have grown accustomed to killing an ant with a hammer. Even when clear indications show dialogue is the best policy, power elites know it would mean accommodating new members in the power club and remain hesitant to admit newcomers. A lack of flexibility or capacity for dialogue creates a need for a hyper-coercive internal security order. An internal security review is underway to make it more coercive. KP has resisted somewhat by introducing the Police Act, 2026, which will bring provincial government oversight over the system, as was required in the KP context, where discord between the police and other institutions has become challenging. But the federal government is resisting it. It seems the power elites will not compromise on the new internal security order and will continue to push their agenda through Nacta or the interior ministry. Foreign policy and geopolitics are sensitive domains for public discourse in the country. The parameters of non-negotiable interests continue to blur and narrow. For the masses, the crisis in the country is no more than a long, tragic soap opera on screen, which they can watch, cry over, and laugh at, but cannot act on. The writer is a security analyst. Published in Dawn, September 27th, 2026
